Attack on Saudi Arabia's King Fahd airport kills two people
By Al Jazeera Staff and Reuters — Published On 22 Oct 2026

Saudi Arabia's General Authority of Civil Aviation (GACA) reported that an attack on King Fahd International Airport in Dammam resulted in two deaths—a Saudi national and an Indian resident—along with eight wounded individuals.

The assault occurred Wednesday and represented the latest in a series of strikes against Saudi infrastructure. On the same day, air defenses also intercepted a drone targeting Saudi Aramco's Shaybah oilfield, resulting in two additional fatalities, according to the Ministry of Energy.

Recent weeks have witnessed escalating violence. On October 11, a projectile struck Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport, killing one and injuring 11. Days earlier, on October 10, another attack on the same airport claimed 12 lives and injured over 300 people.

These incidents coincide with intensifying conflict between Houthi forces and the Saudi-backed Yemeni government. In response to the threat, "the US State Department ordered diplomats and family members to depart from its missions in Saudi Arabia" on Wednesday, with similar withdrawals planned from other regional US missions.
